MECHANISM — WHAT I CAN SUPPORT (the "pure tailwind rolls it north" story is refuted, and the east component is now explained):
1. It is REAL motion in the simulator's truth state, not an estimator artefact. Dataflash SIM.Lat/Lng (SITL truth) and POS.Lat/Lng (EKF) agree to <0.05 m at the first logged sample, both at (+3.756 N, +3.553 E) m. [HV4W55S_spawn_probe.json]
2. The creep is locked to the BODY X AXIS, not to the wind. Over 11 consecutive pre-arm steps the displacement-increment bearing tracks the aircraft's own contemporaneous heading with residual median -0.32 deg, max |residual| 1.00 deg, while the heading swings from 19.2 to 84.3 deg. Step size constant at 0.407-0.425 m per wall second (HV_SPEEDUP=5 => 0.084 m/s of simulated time); observed path 4.648 m, net chord 4.338 m. A wind-driven slide would hold one fixed bearing; it does not. [HV4W55S_spawn_arc.json]
=> THE ~44 deg BEARING IS THE CHORD OF AN ARC. The ~3.5 m east component is simply the part of the arc flown after the nose had swung past 45 deg. It is NOT a separate eastward force, and it is not "unexplained" any more.
3. The rotation is a WEATHERVANE, on the ground. Over B2's 445.0 s parked-and-armed window the truth yaw rises monotonically 126.91 -> 179.45 deg, i.e. the nose settles pointing at SIM_WIND_DIR = 180 (the FROM direction). SIM.Alt is constant at 100.09 m (ground) and truth roll/pitch are 0.0 throughout; truth position moves only a further 0.31 m N / 0.25 m E in that window — once the nose leaves the downwind quarter the creep stops, which is also why it stops near 5 m (at ~90 deg heading the forward wind component is zero).
4. Source support (ArduPilot SITL copy inside this repo, runs/artifacts/AIRFRAME_SIM_MODEL/s1b/review2/tree_3deee9c/): SIM_Aircraft.cpp:787-803 ground branch is explicitly "zero roll/pitch, but keep yaw", and dcm has already been rotated by this step's aero moment before the clamp, so free yaw on the ground is by design. Yaw moment na = qbar*b*(c_n_0 + c_n_b*beta + ...) (SIM_Plane.cpp:350) with beta = atan2f(velocity_air_bf.y, velocity_air_bf.x) (SIM_Plane.cpp:484): a pure tailwind gives velocity_air_bf = (-W,0,0) so beta = atan2(0,-W) = +180 deg exactly (the atan2 branch cut) — the largest possible beta, hence the largest possible yaw moment; a pure crosswind (the 270 deg cells) gives beta = -90 deg, half as large.

MECHANISM — WHAT I CANNOT SUPPORT (said plainly in the annotation):
- The MAGNITUDE of the creep is not derived. That same snapshot's SIM_QuadPlane.cpp:34 selects GROUND_BEHAVIOR_NO_MOVEMENT, whose branch zeroes velocity_ef.x/.y every step, i.e. under that source the aircraft should not translate at all. The observed behaviour (body-forward only, lateral zero, yaw free) looks like GROUND_BEHAVIOR_FWD_ONLY (SIM_Plane.cpp:84, SIM_Aircraft.cpp:806-845) instead.
- I cannot prove the running sitl/ArduPlane.exe (2026-04-07, 10930117 B, sha256 dec596c865ac2e4a056d7d159d79b33ab957b7d36bcb5a0cf252815e922f0913) was built from that snapshot, and SIM_GND_BEHAV (default -1 = no override) appears nowhere on the --defaults chain. So WHICH ground branch runs is still open.
- IMU specific force could not be used as evidence: the dataflash only starts at arming, by which time the creep had stopped (parked IMU.AccX/AccY medians -0.001/-0.001 m/s2, horizontal magnitude 0.0014 m/s2). Settling it would need a controlled SITL probe (SIM_GND_BEHAV sweep, or LOG_DISARMED=1), which the one-sortie-at-a-time rule ruled out.

WHY 270 deg IS BENIGN (same gate, same code, same stations, recomputed): HV4W00 0.022/0.022/0.030 m @ 181/180/222 deg (that is the 1e-7 deg ~1.1 cm quantisation noise floor); HV4W05, HV4W55 and HV4W55R all 0.134/0.183/0.215 m @ 99.6/90.0/87.0 deg (due east = the direction the air moves for a 270 deg wind); BEAMIDP1 0.022/0.022/0.030 m. A 270 deg wind on a north-facing parked aircraft is a pure crosswind: the relative flow lies on the body y axis, which the ground model zeroes, and its yaw moment is half. The three 270 deg sorties reproduce the same triple bit-for-bit, which supports "SITL is deterministic here".

SIGNED WIND RULE FOR 180 deg — WHICH RULE AND WHY: the survey strips run east-west, so a 5 m/s wind FROM 180 is a pure crosswind on them and the east-minus-west asymmetry is ~0 BY CONSTRUCTION — and "~0" is also exactly what "the wind never reached the simulator" looks like, so it cannot serve as the test. The rule therefore moves to the north-south legs, with east-minus-west required to return to zero as a second condition. Measured (windaxis.py, same metric/filters as the c2 probe, bins 90 deg wide centred on each axis):
  north-minus-south +9.90 / +9.68 / +9.61 m/s  (rule: +2W = +10.0 +/- 1.0 AND positive, because a wind FROM 180 moves the air north so northbound legs are faster) — PASS, correct sign.
  east-minus-west   -0.02 / -0.02 / -0.01 m/s  (rule: 0 +/- 1.0) — PASS.
The axes swap cleanly against the controls: HV4W55/HV4W55R (FROM 270) give east-minus-west +9.96..+9.98 and north-minus-south -0.5..-1.3; HV4W00 (no wind) reads +0.38..+0.46 on all four bins with both differences ~0. So the test is not "any east-west asymmetry means wind", it is "the asymmetry appears on the axis the wind should put it on".
Independent cross-check, the FC's own EKF wind (dataflash NKF2/XKF2 VWN/VWE medians, avoiding the broken wrapping-angle mean): 4.952 / 4.852 / 4.881 m/s FROM 179.5 / 180.0 / 179.3 deg (rule 180 +/- 20).
